national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP); taxpayer portal: impots.gouv.fr; corporate e-filing and registration gateway: pro.impots.gouv.fr; single business formalities portal: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique Electronique).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL is incorporated through the Guichet Unique Electronique; the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce transmits the application to INSEE, which issues the national identifier SIREN and establishment identifier SIRET. The local Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) automatically assigns the intra-Community VAT number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) usually within 2 weeks of registration, based on Article 286 of the CGI. A foreign entity without a French fixed establishment that carries out taxable transactions in France must apply directly to the DGFiP/SIE for a French VAT number; non-EU applicants must appoint an accredited fiscal representative (représentant fiscal) unless a specific derogation applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box exists in France. Available elections: (1) Option for Impôt sur le Revenu (IR) under Article 239 bis AA CGI for an eligible PME (fewer than 50 employees and turnover not exceeding EUR 10M), valid for 5 years, including the SARL de famille regime under Article 239 bis AA/AB CGI; (2) default corporate income tax (IS) applies absent the IR option; (3) group VAT single taxpayer election ('assujetti unique') under Article 256 C CGI for closely linked entities; (4) option for the franchise en base de TVA small-business exemption where turnover thresholds are met; (5) ATAD 2 hybrid-mismatch election/notification obligations under Articles 212 bis CGI.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA); EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC transposed into Articles 256 to 283 of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold: a French-established SARL exercising any taxable activity must be VAT-registered from the first euro. The small-business exemption ('franchise en base de TVA') applies to established taxpayers below EUR 85,000 (goods) and EUR 37,500 (services) for 2025, but this is an exemption, not a registration threshold. For non-established EU/foreign suppliers of B2C distance sales of goods, the EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold applies (OSS special scheme); for B2B supply of works on immovable property located in France (rope-access façade repairs), registration or reverse charge applies from the first euro without threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing a phased mandatory e-invoicing reform: all established taxable persons must receive structured e-invoices from 1 September 2026 and issue them from 1 September 2026 for large enterprises and from 1 September 2027 for ETIs and SMEs/PMEs. Transmission must occur via the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or a certified Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) using structured formats (Factur-X, UBL, CII) compliant with EN 16931 / Peppol BIS 3.0. The reform also imposes mandatory e-reporting (données de transactions et de paiements) to DGFiP. France does not operate real-time pre-clearance digital stamping; issuance is transmitted after the transaction with periodic settlement, but the fiscal data transmission obligation is mandatory and automated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods outside the European Union are taxable at 0% (exonération) under Article 262 I CGI provided the goods physically leave the EU and the exporter retains proof of export. However, the core commercial scope — rope-access structural glass replacement and façade works on supertall skyscrapers located in France — constitutes a supply of services connected with immovable property situated in France under Article 259 A 1° CGI; therefore the place of supply is France and the services are subject to French TVA at the standard rate of 20% (or, where contractually eligible, the 10% reduced rate for certain renovation works on residential premises older than two years). These domestic immovable-property services do not qualify as zero-rated exports. For other services rendered to foreign clients where the place of supply is outside France under Articles 259, 259 A to 259 D CGI (e.g., B2B general rule: customer established outside France and outside the EU), the supply falls outside the scope of French VAT, and corresponding input VAT recovery follows ordinary refund procedures.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Déclaration en Douane / Export Customs Declaration (DAE) with registered MRU number
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill / CMR road consignment note proving physical exit from EU
Commercial invoice and export packing list
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank credit confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Incoterms-based contract and transport documents proving transfer of risk and control to the foreign purchaser
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The tax administration may verify export substantiation within the standard 3-year review period (6 years for fraud/aggravated situations) under Article L. 176 of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales. Unsupported or fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger retroactive VAT reassessment, monthly late-payment interest of 0.20% (intérêt de retard), a 40% negligence penalty under Article 1728 CGI, or an 80% bad-faith penalty under Article 1729 CGI. Criminal exposure under Article 1741 CGI for tax/misdeclaration fraud includes imprisonment up to 3 years and a fine up to EUR 45,000 (aggravated organized fraud: up to 5 years and EUR 100,000), in addition to corporate criminal sanctions. Export and VAT records must be retained for 10 years under Article L. 102 B of the LPF.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting as the Eurozone national central bank, balance-of-payments statistics authority, and administrator of the cross-border fund-transfer declaration framework under the Code monétaire et financier; ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) as the French banking licensor and AML-CFT prudential supervisor; European Central Bank (ECB) as supreme monetary authority of the eurozone; Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) as the enforcement authority for cross-border fund-transfer declarations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a fully liberalised Eurozone jurisdiction: both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible, with no exchange-control licensing, no repatriation authorisation, and no quantitative limits. A French SARL may lawfully hold foreign-currency accounts and remit dividends or profits to non-resident shareholders without FX approval. The residual compliance burden is purely documentary: (i) every cross-border payment through the French banking system must carry a Banque de France balance-of-payments purpose code (direct investment, construction service, or goods classification); (ii) any transfer of funds to or from France exceeding EUR 10,000 triggers the Article L152-1 Code monétaire et financier declaration obligation (CERFA n°14008 filed with DGDDI for transported cash or evidenced via the bank for wire transfers); (iii) profit-remittance dossiers should contain audited financial statements, filed tax returns, and withholding-tax certificates. No capital controls target the rope-access facade construction sector; convertibility friction is effectively zero, but documentary artefacts must be pre-agreed with the bank to avoid settlement delay.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. France abolished all export-proceeds surrender requirements as part of full exchange-control liberalisation. A French SARL is free to collect export receivables in EUR or any convertible currency, retain them abroad, hold foreign-currency accounts at EEA-licensed banks, and convert at market rates without central-bank approval. The sole mandatory duty is statistical: export transactions must be tagged with the correct Banque de France balance-of-payments code (100-series for goods; 200-series for services; direct-investment category where works abroad constitute a permanent establishment), with periodic electronic reporting to the Banque de France balance-of-payments service. No conversion ratio applies to export proceeds; a bank confirmation evidencing the underlying export operation is sufficient for customs and statistical purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium-High for operational euro rails; Low for capital escrow, documentary LCs, supply-chain trade finance, and FX hedging. Legal constraints: an offshore non-EEA digital EMI cannot lawfully provide payment services to a French SARL or hold client funds for it absent an ACPR licence or a valid EEA passport; only ACPR- or EEA-authorised EMIs (e.g., Qonto, Shine, Wise Business, Revolut Business) may onboard French corporate clients, and only for payment and e-money activity. Such EMIs may never hold capital-contribution escrow funds (fonds de séquestre), may not issue documentary letters of credit, and may not structure ISDA/EMIR-cleared FX derivatives. The treasury blueprint therefore designates the French Tier-1 bank as the sole clearing, escrow, LC, and hedging node, with EMIs deployed only as supplementary rails for same-day SEPA disbursements and low-value progress payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law (Code monétaire et financier, ACPR AML-CFT guidelines, and digital-identity provisions introduced by Law n°2019-486 / PACTE) permits fully remote onboarding via ACPR-compliant video identification and electronic signatures. In practice, incumbent Tier-1 French banks require at least one face-to-face underwriting interview (rendez-vous de souscription) with the SARL gérant and any non-resident UBOs, and physical execution of the bank’s signature card before SWIFT/SEPA instruction rights and corporate cards are activated. Remote-only opening is reliably available at fintech EMIs and selected neo-bank programmes. For a cross-border SARL with non-resident shareholders, the lowest-friction path remains a short physical visit by the managing director carrying certified passports, original K-bis extract, statutory-licence certificates, and original corporate resolutions. Banks may waive physical presence where a registered French expert-comptable co-signs the account-opening file and confirms the company’s economic substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBOs and directors with no French fiscal footprint, flagging the SARL as a potential shell or conduit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies and three-month proof-of-address (utility bill or bank statement); notarised and, where necessary, legalised/Apostilled corporate resolutions; French beneficial-owner registry (RBE / Registre National des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) filing receipt; directors' CVs with relevant construction-industry track record; registered-office lease and planned payroll documents evidencing substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-altitude rope-access facade activity lacking the required statutory licences and qualifications, triggering the bank's sector-policy review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Extrait K-bis showing ISIC 43.90 and BTP activity; Qualibat or equivalent French construction qualification certificate for high-altitude facade and rope-access works; CACES / travaux-en-hauteur rope-access training attestations for operative personnel; professional civil-liability insurance (responsabilité civile professionnelle) attestation; health-and-safety plan (plan de prévention); and the statutory BTP licence or professional-identity card where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border capital injection and recurring inbound SWIFT flows exceeding the EUR 10,000 declaration threshold, activating source-of-funds investigation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised act of contribution (acte de souscription d'apport) specifying the SARL capital; shareholder board resolution approving the injection; complete bank-statement trail on the transferring shareholder's account including SWIFT MT103 messages; UBO net-worth and source-of-wealth profile; French and non-resident tax reference statements; signed account-opening declaration (OPC) under the French LCB-FT framework.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-list or PEP screening hits, or negative media concerning building-subcontracting chains and high-risk payment corridors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full beneficial-ownership chain disclosure without shell or crypto-vehicle structures; World-Check / Lexis-Nexis screening excerpts for the SARL and all shareholders; clean K-bis extract showing no judicial liquidation, disqualification, or collective proceedings; contractual chain mapping of facade principals and glass-supplier counterparties; accountant reference letter confirming absence of adverse indicators.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SARL with an empty balance sheet and no filed tax returns, failing the bank's economic-substance standard.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan and 24-month cash-flow forecast grounded in signed rope-access facade contracts or letters of intent; registered-office ownership or lease evidence; engagement letter of the French expert-comptable; professional insurance certificates; ultimate-parent group structure where applicable; and an aged transaction forecast demonstrating the Stage-4 progress-billing and wire-transfer cycle.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injection is routed via SWIFT MT103 (or, for euro-origin flows, SEPA Credit Transfer) from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the SARL's EUR IBAN at the French Tier-1 bank. The payment purpose field must state the capital character, e.g., 'Apport en capital / Capital contribution – FR_SARL'; the receiving bank must classify the flow under the Banque de France balance-of-payments direct-investment category (equity-capital contribution), and where the portal mandates an ISO 20022 purpose code, 'CAPC' (Capital Contribution) must be inserted so the credit is booked as equity rather than trade or treasury flow. The compliance verification pack comprises the notarised contribution act, shareholder resolution, the transferring shareholder's bank statements evidencing the debit cascade, and the receiving bank's source-of-funds validation for any inbound transfer exceeding EUR 10,000. For USD/CHF injections, the French bank may credit a foreign-currency account and convert via spot at market rate; no exchange-control authorisation is required, but the direct-investment BOP tag and the Article L152-1 declaration duty remain mandatory.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant via EBA CLEARING / TARGET2 for eurozone subcontractors, glazing suppliers, and progress-ACH milestone invoices; (ii) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers with MT202 cover for USD, CHF, GBP, and CNH trade settlements through the French bank's correspondent network; (iii) irrevocable commercial documentary Letters of Credit (UCP 600) and standby LCs (ISP98) issued by the French Tier-1 bank for import of structural glass, aluminium facade units, and high-altitude access equipment, with the required document set of commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading or AWB, CMR, certificate of origin, and insurance certificate; (iv) for US-facing vendors, disbursements route via Fedwire or CHIPS through the correspondent tier, using US ACH only where the vendor maintains a US clearing-member account; (v) demand guarantees and bid bonds issued via the SWIFT network to support international facade tenders. Every outbound disbursement must carry the accurate Banque de France balance-of-payments code (construction services in the 200-series; material imports in the 100-series) to ensure customs clearance, correct statistical reporting, and clean audit trails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC deliverable EUR FX outright forwards (change à terme) against USD, GBP, CHF, and CNH under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or French FBF Master Agreement, covering invoice, procurement, and milestone-payment exposures up to 12 months

EUR/USD and EUR/CNH cross-currency swaps, including cross-currency interest-rate swaps, for matching large facade contracts and equipment-finance liabilities, documented under ISDA/CSA with bilateral margin
Vanilla currency options (call/put on EUR/USD and EUR/CNH) purchased for asymmetric protection during competitive international tenders
FX swaps (spot-forward combinations) for short-term treasury liquidity management without synthetic EUR re-denomination

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) solely for currencies with onshore convertibility restrictions (e.g., CNY where the onshore market is unavailable to French corporate treasuries), subject to the French bank's internal product-eligibility gate, EMIR reporting, and margin rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholders' ordinary general meeting approving the annual accounts and allocation of results
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office records; minute book 'registre des décisions des associés'
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the financial year-end (for a 31 December year-end: by 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No government filing fee; dividends paid without approved accounts are null, and the managing partner is exposed to civil liability and a court application for compulsory winding-up in cases of persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of the annual accounts with the Commercial Court Registry (dépôt des comptes annuels au greffe)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (RCS file; publication in BODACC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months of the financial year-end (31 December year-end: by 31 July); extension of up to three months obtainable by court order only in exceptional justified circumstances.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a registrar's formal notice, surcharge for late payment of registry fees, criminal fine of up to EUR 15,000 on the manager, exclusion from beneficial public procurement, and eventual administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and liasse fiscale (formulaire 2065-SD with schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (Service des impôts des entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year SARL: by the second working day after 1 May, or by the third working day after 1 June when filed through a certified accountant; non-calendar year SARL: within three months of year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the company to a 10% penalty on the corporate tax due under Article 1728 CGI, increased to 40% for bad faith, plus monthly late-payment interest under Article 1727 CGI, and the tax authority's summary tax assessment powers.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard income tax rate); 25.83% where the 3.3% corporate surcharge applies to income tax exceeding EUR 763,000.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for eligible SMEs with turnover below EUR 10 million; accelerated depreciation for safety and environmental equipment; French research tax credit (CIR) applicable to certified R&D in rope-access engineering.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (Déclaration de Résultats) and supplementary schedules 2050-SD through 2059-SD, filed electronically via the professional taxpayer portal of impots.gouv.fr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly prepayments are due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December when the prior-year corporate income tax exceeds EUR 2,100.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending on 31 December: second working day after 1 May. For non-calendar fiscal year-end: second working day after the third month following the closing date. Cessation declaration must be filed within 60 days of the cessation of operations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter French legal form (SARL), legal name, registered address, RCS and SIREN/SIRET numbers, French APE/NAF code corresponding to ISIC 4390, and a concise description of the rope-access facade activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARL must enter the French permanent establishment address when French operations constitute a taxable PE. If no French PE is present, complete the block with the foreign head office identification and state that treaty protection is claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Specify the accounting period opened and closed, duration in months, and confirm the number of consecutive periods if a short first fiscal year applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a French PE, the accounting period should be consistent with the French statutory books; where the foreign main fiscal year differs, an auxiliary French accounting statement is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List fixed assets: rope access platforms, lifting equipment, mobile scaffolding, personal protective equipment, vehicles and office equipment, including acquisition cost, cumulative depreciation and potential revaluation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fixed assets economically used by the French PE must appear on the PE's French balance sheet; equipment temporarily imported from abroad should be reported separately where title remains with the foreign head office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Record tax-deductible provisions for litigations, guarantees, bad debts and maintenance obligations on facade contracts, ensuring the provisions meet the criteria of probability, specificity and attachment to the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE provisions are accepted only when a contractual and legal obligation is attributable to the French operations; group-level head-office charges must be re-invoiced under transfer pricing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter tax loss carryforwards by fiscal year and calculate the current-year deductible portion under the statutory offset cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French PE's losses may be carried forward in France only if the PE itself is not treaty-exempt; the foreign head office cannot apply French losses against home-country revenue unless the applicable DTA grants credit or permits fiscal unity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% increase of net tax due if no formal notice, 40% after 30 days of formal notice, and 80% for fraudulent concealment. Late payment incurs a 5% surcharge plus 0.20% monthly interest. Additional penalties arise where the assessed base exceeds actual base by more than 50% or where bookkeeping is manifestly irregular.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on distributions to non-resident corporate shareholders under Article 119 bis 2 CGI; 12.8% for non-resident individuals, plus social levies where applicable.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA rate, the beneficial owner must provide a residence certificate (France obtains this from tax administrations under the applicable DTA, commonly the Formulaire 5000 or its exchange equivalent) before payment, or file a refund claim after withholding. Under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, no French withholding tax applies if the parent holds at least 5% of the SARL for at least 24 months, provided the arrangement is not artificial and the parent has substantive economic activity.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for patents, trademarks and technical know-how paid to non-residents carry a statutory 33.33% withholding; DTA rates generally range from 0% to 10%, and the EU Interest & Royalties Directive may eliminate withholding when a 25% direct shareholding or voting right has been held for two years. Interest on bonds and certain movable receivables carries a statutory 25% withholding, but arm's-length interest paid to a bank or on commercial trade credit is usually exempt from French withholding; DTA rates commonly range from 0% to 10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 (French entity or group annual revenue or gross assets) for mandatory Master File and Local File; EU CBCR obligation at EUR 750,000,000 group consolidated turnover. Below the mandatory threshold, contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation must still be maintained and produced within 30 days of a French tax authority request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not maintain a stand-alone Economic Substance Regulations statute; however, the abuse-of-law doctrine under Article L.64 LPF and the EU ATAD substance requirements deny treaty benefits, interest deductions and royalty exemptions to entities lacking real economic substance. A rope-access facade SARL must demonstrate French operational direction, local employees, owned or leased equipment, active decision-making and effective business functions in France; a mailbox SARL with a foreign nominee manager and no French activity can be recharacterised as a sham and subjected to 80% penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-invoicing facade contracts, suppressing revenue from high-altitude rope-access jobs, paying technicians in cash without social declarations, issuing fictitious subcontractor invoices, or booking unrelated personal expenses as French operating costs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 1741 CGI imposes up to five years imprisonment and a EUR 750,000 fine, increased to EUR 2 million in aggravated cases; administrative fines of 40% to 80% of the recharacterized base plus 0.20% monthly late interest are assessed simultaneously.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant may be personally prosecuted for fraud, receive a travel ban and management prohibition, be ordered to pay the tax debt and interest under the action for corporate deficit contribution, and suffer seizure of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Artificial Profit Absorbing Structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a French SARL without local office, staff, equipment or real business risk; channelling contract proceeds through a foreign affiliate; invoicing excessive group fees, royalties or financing charges to drain French taxable profit while decision-making is kept abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: French anti-abuse procedure permits recharacterization of transactions, disallowance of deductions, recapture of the entire tax advantage, and a penalty of up to 80% in cases of sham or fictitious contracts. Judicial dissolution may be sought where the SARL is found to be a mere shell harming creditors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The de jure gérant and the shadow director are jointly liable for the resulting tax debt and interest; they may be disqualified from managing a business for up to 15 years, subjected to travel bans, and held civilly liable in liquidation proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-Filing, False Filing and Beneficial Ownership Concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to submit Form 2065-SD and annexed schedules by the statutory deadline; non-disclosure of foreign bank accounts or foreign assets; false beneficial ownership declarations; use of nominee shareholders to hide the real economic beneficiary.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Relevant sanctions: 10% to 80% increase of assessed tax, 0.20% monthly interest, automatic assessment where no return is filed, EUR 1,500 fine per undisclosed foreign bank account (EUR 10,000 for non-cooperative jurisdictions), and criminal penalties for fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Persistent false filings may constitute fraudulent bankruptcy or criminal fraud; directors risk civil attachment on personal assets, personal disqualification, prohibition from holding a commercial passport, and imprisonment where intentional concealment is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation Between Related Undertakings
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling high-altitude maintenance services below cost to a related foreign entity, paying above-market fees to a related B.V. or Luxembourg holding, charging business opportunity commissions, or misallocating profit between the French SARL and the foreign parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The French tax administration may adjust profits using an arm's length method, recharacterise undocumented payments as distributions, impose a 40% bad-faith or 80% fraud penalty, levy EUR 10,000 documentation penalties, and charge 0.20% monthly interest on the extra tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign artificial transfer pricing contracts or allow fraudulent documentation are exposed to civil liability for the tax and penalties, and to criminal sanctions as co-authors of fraud if they personally controlled the scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Distribution, Thin-Capitalization and Disguised Deemed Dividends
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using excessive shareholder loans, interest push-downs or royalty schemes to distribute profits as pseudo-debt while the French SARL never pays formal dividends; making distributions without complying with commercial-law formalities and without withholding French tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The administration may deny interest deductibility under the French thin-capitalization rules, recharacterize excessive interest or royalties as deemed dividends under Article 109-1 CGI, and apply the 25% withholding tax plus 40% penalties and 0.20% monthly interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Gérants who approve abusive distributions in bad faith are jointly liable for missed withholding tax and social debts; in insolvency proceedings the court may order contribution to liabilities, issue a personal bankruptcy order, and impose a management ban of up to 15 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting substantial progress-payment deposits in cash or through unverified accounts, routing payments via shell banks in prohibited jurisdictions, concealing the ultimate owner of project proceeds, or performing facade works for sanctioned state-owned entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: French AML law imposes criminal fines up to EUR 5 million, imprisonment up to five years, and ACPR administrative sanctions including licence withdrawal and asset freezes; independent administrative fines may reach 10% of annual turnover.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners face automatic criminal liability for laundering the proceeds of tax fraud; travel bans and seizure of assets are common, and directors may be held jointly for restitution of illicit transfers plus monetary penalties.
